name: Binglao Poker
description: Binglao is a high-action Pot Limit Omaha (PLO) variant where the deal parameters are randomized before each hand. By rolling a six-sided die, the dealer determines the number of hole cards each player receives (4, 5, or 6) and whether the game will be played as High-only or High-Low 8-or-Better. Popularized in the Nordic poker community and featured in the Norwegian Poker Championship, it requires players to master multiple Omaha formats and adapt their ranges instantly.

history.origins: Developed within the Nordic tournament poker circuit as a way to increase variety and skill testing in mixed-game festivals. It gained official recognition when it was added to the side-event schedule of the Norwegian Poker Championship week in Dublin.
timeline: 2010s: Binglao appears as a novelty '6-Max' side event in European tournaments.
2015: Becomes a recurring feature of the Nordic mixed-game rotation.
Present: Played both as a tournament specialty and a high-stakes cash game format in specialized card rooms.
history.cultural: Reflects the Norwegian community's enthusiasm for complex Pot Limit games, where position and range calculation are highly prized.
history.evolution: Binglao is part of the 'Omaha-plus' trend, where increasing the number of hole cards (5-card and 6-card variants) has become popular to create more drawing opportunities and multi-way action.

setup.players: Typically 2 to 6 players; the 6-max format is standard to accommodate the potential for 6 hole cards per player.
setup.dealing: The dealer rolls the D6 to establish the hand rules. Players are dealt 4, 5, or 6 hole cards face down. Five community cards are dealt in the flop (3), turn (1), and river (1) pattern.
setup.equipment: Standard pack, poker chips, one six-sided die (D6).

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest hand (or best qualifying low hand in Hi-Lo deals) at showdown, or by forcing all opponents to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Format Roll**: Dealer rolls die: 1-2 = 4-card, 3-4 = 5-card, 5-6 = 6-card. High/Low is determined by house rule or second roll. 2. **Betting**: Standard Pot Limit structure. 3. **Hand Construction**: You MUST use exactly two cards from your hand and exactly three cards from the community board to form a five-card hand.
keyRules: Pot Limit: The maximum bet or raise is equal to the current total pot.
Qualifying Low: In Hi-Lo rounds, a low hand must consist of five unpaired cards ranked 8 or lower to be eligible.
Scooping: A player who holds both the best high hand and the best qualifying low hand wins the entire pot.

strategy.basic: In 5-card and 6-card rounds, hand equities are much closer. You need very strong 'nut' draws to continue, as opponents are more likely to have connected with the board.
strategy.intermediate: Range Adaptation: Tighten your requirements in 4-card rounds where big pairs are more dominant. In 6-card rounds, look for 'wraps' (sequences of four or more cards) that give you dozens of outs to a straight.
strategy.advanced: Quartering Risk: In Hi-Lo deals, be cautious when playing for the 'Low' half of the pot if you don't have the absolute nuts, as you risk splitting that half with another player while losing the high half.
tips: Master the math of '2 hand + 3 board' before playing—many beginners mistakenly try to use three cards from their hand.
In 6-max format, position is your greatest asset; act last to control the sizing of the pot.

variations.name: High-Only Binglao
variations.description: The High-Low option is removed from the die roll outcomes.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: High-only version is described but engine-level overrides for removing low split logic are not yet encoded.

scoring.description: Standard poker pot mechanics. In High deals, best hand wins entire pot. In Hi-Lo deals, pot is split between best high hand and best qualifying low hand.
scoring.winCondition: Highest chip total at the end of the session or tournament.

synthesis.shortDescription: A wild Pot Limit Omaha variant from the Norwegian tournament circuit. Before each hand, the dealer rolls a 6-sided die to determine how many hole cards you get (4, 5, or 6) AND whether the game is High-only or High-Low. Adapt your strategy every single deal.
